meta.title: Start, find, stop and restart stacks from the terminal today

security.label: Step with an evidenced pain point

nodes.label: devhost start [names]
nodes.explanation: People and agents start with devhost start [names] in a project folder, in the foreground by default or with --detach. In a folder without a manifest the only answer is 'Could not find devhost.toml from <folder> upward.' and 'Run devhost from your project folder, or pass --manifest <path>.': the person is in their project folder, and nothing creates a manifest or links the docs. The Quickstart in devhost --help starts with Caddy setup and 'devhost start  # run the stack in devhost.toml', and start --help has no examples. Every AGENT=1 help screen opens with 'ALERT: Agents must read AGENT=1 devhost skill before using this tool.', but devhost skill prints only an npx install command and a GitHub URL on the main branch: not the guidance, and not the version of this binary (stack-run-stop-12).

sources.label: Searches upward to the repository root
Skill command and the agent help alert

nodes.label: Find + validate manifest
nodes.explanation: Before anything runs, devhost start reads the manifest and its includes, validates the schema, checks the requested names and orders the services by dependsOn. The stack then claims every fixed port and hostname, so a second stack cannot take them. A detached start hands the same validated arguments to a background supervisor. Any check that fails here ends the start with exit 1 before a service runs.

sources.label: Read, validate, check names; --detach
Claim fixed ports and hostnames

nodes.label: Start + health-check
nodes.sublabel: one by one; pass or fail
nodes.explanation: Services start one after another in dependency order, and each waits for its health check before the next starts. After a short delay devhost prints 'Waiting for service api to pass its HTTP health check on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/healthz (elapsed: 2s; timeout: 30s)...', but the HTTP probe is pass or fail on a 2xx and never keeps the status it got: an API that answers the README's health = { http = "/healthz" } with 404 waits the full 30 s, then fails twice with 'did not pass its health check within 30000ms', never saying the path answered 404 (journey-new-project-03). After a killed stack, the TCP check connects to the orphaned old process, so a new process that failed with EADDRINUSE is reported ready (interrupted-operations-02).

sources.label: Start each service in dependency order
Waiting line with elapsed and timeout
HTTP check keeps only pass or fail

nodes.label: Detached start reports
nodes.explanation: devhost start --detach launches the supervisor in the background, sends its output only to the stack log, and waits. The terminal stays blank for the whole wait: no stack name, no service in progress, no elapsed time. On success it prints 'Started Acme Shop (PID n).', the URLs without service names or the primary marker (the /api/ route first) and the log path; it never names the services a partial start left out. Ctrl-C during the wait prints the log tail and '[ERROR] received SIGINT (Ctrl-C) (signal 2) before the stack was ready', reporting the person's own cancel as an error, and a failed start states its cause twice (stack-run-stop-04).

sources.label: Child writes only to the log; command waits
Started line, bare URLs, log path

nodes.label: Already running, exit 0
nodes.explanation: When the manifest's stack already runs, a detached start reports it and stops: 'Already running Acme Shop (PID n).' and the log path, exit 0, whatever names were asked for; AGENT=1 prints the same. devhost start --detach admin on a stack started with storefront never names admin, which stays not started, and its hostname answers the generic devhost 404 that blames routing. The running stack's URLs are not repeated either. stack-lifecycle.md documents that the selection does not change, but the terminal never tells the person or agent who asked (stack-run-stop-01).

sources.label: Existing stack reported; names not compared
URLs only for a stack it started

nodes.label: Read the stack log
nodes.explanation: The only way to read a detached stack is the printed Log path, <state>/logs/stack-<64 hex>.log, about 100 characters. The file appends every start without timestamps or a run separator, each run in the format of whoever launched it (an AGENT=1 start switches it to 'api: ...' lines mid-file), and after devhost stack restart the stack writes to a new restart-<random>/<old PID>.log while the old path goes silent; each restart leaves another folder (stack-run-stop-05). In the agent format, failures such as 'configuration reload rejected' and 'exited with code 1' carry no ERR: or WARN: marker while warnings do (agent-cli-journey-05). A foreground stack writes no log at all, so an agent cannot read a hot reload's outcome (agent-cli-journey-02). An idle stop of a detached stack is recorded only here (stack-run-stop-11).

sources.label: Log path: logs/stack-<sha256>.log
Restart logs to restart-*/<PID>.log

nodes.label: URL list after slowest
nodes.explanation: A foreground start prints no line as each service starts. The URL lines appear together only after the last service passes its health check: the primary was serving at about 3 s, its URL appeared at about 10 s. No line says the stack is ready or how long it took, the API path route is listed before the primary, then 'not started: ...', and with a chatty service the list scrolls away and is never printed again (stack-run-stop-03). A service that crashed during the start is listed with its URL like the working ones, and the start never says one of six failed (journey-crash-to-fix-05, a duplicate). The stack directory URL never appears (stack-directory-06). Lines are hard-wrapped at the terminal width inside the label gutter, splitting URLs, paths and commands mid-word (stack-run-stop-10). A 40-service stack prints 40 URL lines (stack-scale-07).

sources.label: URL and not-started lists after all start
One line per URL; primary marked
Hard wrap at the terminal width

nodes.label: Service exits, waits
nodes.explanation: While the stack runs, a service that exits prints 'api exited with code 1; devhost is waiting for a restart.', but the CLI cannot restart one service: devhost service restart is an unknown command, every CLI path restarts the whole stack, and help and the skill name only browser buttons (agent-cli-journey-03). A SIGTERM from outside prints only 'exited with code 143', with no signal, time or sender (interrupted-operations-04); a daemon that dies prints nothing at all (manifest-hot-reload-2-02). Nothing shows the command, folder or manifest line behind a crash (journey-crash-to-fix-04). devhost prints the same crash line for stops it made itself: a worktree switch, which also names checkouts by folder (worktree-switch-04), and Restart Stack, while every toolbar Start reprints all URLs and the not-started list (stack-scale-07). A config.toml save prints 'Applied ...' and every URL again, never what changed (proxy-settings-04).

sources.label: Every exit: waiting for a restart
The service command has only list

nodes.label: Open a printed URL
nodes.explanation: People open a printed URL in the browser. A manifest that mounts the API with path = "/api" on the front end's hostname starts without a warning, the API passes its health check (probed on its own port), the terminal prints 'api: https://newapp.localhost/api' and the toolbar shows 2/2 up. But Caddy renders the route as 'handle /api', an exact match, so /api/hello reaches the static site's 404 and the page's fetch fails with a JSON parse error; a path without a host is ignored the same silent way (journey-new-project-01). An HTTP client polling a service during the start gets about 750 KB of 404 HTML before routes exist, then empty 502s (agent-cli-journey-04).

sources.label: Path route renders as handle <path>

nodes.label: stack list / stack find
nodes.explanation: From another terminal, devhost stack list and devhost stack find print '<PID><TAB><manifest path>' and nothing else, exactly the same while a service is crashed: no stack name, foreground or detached, URLs, log or service state. devhost status and devhost logs are unknown commands, and devhost service list reads the manifest on disk, not the running stack (agent-cli-journey-01). stack find matches any query as a substring of a hostname, name or manifest path, so 'devhost stack find .' or the project's folder returns every stack below it, worktrees included, while a relative folder path returns nothing; two stacks named Acme Shop print only as PID and path (stack-run-stop-08). Neither prints the stack directory URL (stack-directory-06).

sources.label: PID, tab and manifest path only
Substring match on host, name and path

nodes.label: devhost stop [--worktrees]
nodes.explanation: devhost stop finds the stack through any path to its manifest and prints 'Stopping 1 active stack process(es) associated with manifest...', 'Sending SIGTERM to process 84244...' and 'Process 84244 stopped cleanly.': no stack name, a worktree hint before the action naming no stack, and stdout although reference/output.md says stop progress goes to stderr (stack-run-stop-06, agent-cli-journey-05). When the stack takes longer than 15 s, stop SIGKILLs only the supervisor, prints 'Process n terminated.' and exits 0 while its services keep running (interrupted-operations-01). --worktrees stops every stack in the repository one after another with no list first and no confirmation (stack-run-stop-07); it gives up at the first stack it cannot stop, exiting 1 on that PID without trying or naming the rest (stack-run-stop-14), and stops nothing while any running stack's folder is gone, even another repository's, failing on a raw Git error (stack-run-stop-16). Running chat conversations end without a word (chat-conversations-03). devhost caddy stop takes every stack offline with one line, 'managed caddy stopped.', naming none (notices-and-feedback-04).

sources.label: Worktree hint, PID lines, --worktrees loop
SIGTERM, 15 s, SIGKILL the supervisor
Git per stack folder; errors end --worktrees

nodes.label: devhost stack restart
nodes.explanation: devhost stack restart (--all after an upgrade) sends each stack SIGTERM, waits a fixed 15 s and relaunches the same command detached from this executable, logging to a new restart-<random>/<old PID>.log. A slower shutdown (two services each using their 10 s grace) makes it print 'stack is still stopping after 15s; replacement was not started', naming a log no replacement writes, and exit 1: the stack ends stopped, nothing replaces it, and no start command is printed (stack-run-stop-13). --all restarts every stack and serve session with 'Restarting Acme Shop (PID n); log: ...' lines that cannot be told apart when two checkouts share a name, ending 'Restarted ...; services may still be starting.' Neither it nor stop --worktrees lists what it will affect first, asks for confirmation or offers a dry run (stack-run-stop-07). A stack whose manifest is saved, even unchanged, after --all captured it is refused with 'stack ownership changed; refresh worktrees', a toolbar instruction, and keeps the old executable; one that stopped meanwhile counts as failed (stack-run-stop-15). A foreground stack it replaces ends its terminal like an ordinary shutdown (stack-run-stop-02).

sources.label: Every live stack with --all; no preview
SIGTERM, wait, relaunch detached
Refused when the record changed since capture

nodes.label: Stop every service
nodes.explanation: Ctrl-C, devhost stop, stack restart and the idle timeout all end here. The supervisor sends SIGTERM to every service, then waits for them one at a time, up to 10 s each, and sends SIGKILL to any still running, so two slow services cost 20 s, and the Stopped lines print only after the slowest (interrupted-operations-03). Every stop path also signals every PID the service's tracker ever recorded and still finds alive, without checking it is the same process: stopping a long-running service can kill unrelated processes that reused its old child PIDs (process-containment-01). After every service has stopped, the supervisor can still hang with no time limit on a Caddy reload (stack-scale-01). Then it releases its hostnames, ports and routes, and unregisters the stack last.

sources.label: TERM all, wait each up to 10 s, KILL
Signals every tracked PID still alive
Tracked PIDs are only ever added

nodes.label: Shutdown lines, exit
nodes.explanation: In the foreground terminal Ctrl-C prints 'Received SIGINT (Ctrl-C) (signal 2); shutting down the stack.' and one 'Stopping service <name>...' per service. A second Ctrl-C only echoes ^C: the supervisor reads one signal. The terminal then stays silent for 20 s or more while slow services are waited for; force-killed services print 'Stopped service <name>.' like clean stops, and services that exited minutes earlier are stopped again (interrupted-operations-03). A devhost stack restart from another terminal prints exactly this shutdown and exits 143 without saying the stack was replaced, and devhost start in this terminal then fails naming an included manifest first (stack-run-stop-02). An idle timeout prints 'Idle timeout of 30s reached. Automatically shutting down the stack...' and exits 0.

sources.label: Reads one signal; a second is ignored
Stopping and Stopped service lines
Stack stopped. after cleanup

nodes.label: Generic 404 page
nodes.explanation: After any stop, and after an idle timeout nobody saw, the app's hostname answers Caddy's generic page: 'No active devhost route matched this hostname.' with the hint to check that the stack is running. It names no stack, stop reason or time, and no command or folder that starts it again; a detached start never mentioned the idle timeout, which only its log records (stack-run-stop-11).

sources.label: Idle timeout shuts the stack down
Generic 404 title and hint

nodes.label: Start refused
nodes.explanation: Errors that stop a start name no file, line or next step: an unknown key in an included manifest prints 'Manifest schema is invalid:' and 'services.admin Unrecognized key: "hostname"' with no file and no 'did you mean host'; a TOML error names the line after the mistake behind the parser's prefix; a hostname clash names only the first clash and a PID, and the next appears only after fixing it; an unknown name lists services and groups mixed and points to devhost service list, which omits groups (stack-run-stop-09; a hot reload rejection has the same gap, manifest-hot-reload-03, a duplicate). A wrong cwd fails first with a raw git error from worktree discovery, so the documented services.<name>.cwd message is never reached (journey-new-project-04). With AGENT=1, ERR: marks only the first line of a multi-line error (agent-cli-journey-05). The person fixes the file and runs devhost start again.

sources.label: Schema errors: heading and key paths only
Git discovery runs before the cwd check
Agent mode: one ERR: prefix

nodes.label: Services outlive stack
nodes.explanation: When the supervisor dies first (devhost stop's 15 s SIGKILL, a force-closed terminal, kill -9 or a crash), every service lives on in its own process group under PID 1 and keeps answering its hostname, while devhost stack list prints nothing and a second devhost stop reports no stack (interrupted-operations-01). The next devhost start drops the dead stack's records without a word; services on fixed ports fail with EADDRINUSE, yet their health checks connect to the orphans, the start lists their URLs as ready and only then reports the exits (interrupted-operations-02). Recovery means finding and killing the old processes by hand.

sources.label: SIGKILL reaches only the supervisor
Dead stack's records dropped silently
TCP check passes on any listener

cards.title: What already works
items: devhost start finds devhost.toml from any folder up to the repository root; stop, stack find and stack restart accept any path to the manifest
Every start is validated before a service runs, and hostname and fixed-port claims keep a second stack from taking them
A detached start waits for readiness, reuses a stack that already runs, serializes concurrent starts with a per-manifest lock, and on failure prints the log tail and stops what it started
A slow health check prints a waiting line with the elapsed time and the timeout
A failed service leaves the rest of the stack running (the recovery contract)
Ctrl-C names its signal, and every stop releases hostnames, ports and routes before it unregisters the stack
stack restart stops nothing when the executable is unavailable or the stack is its own ancestor
devhost stop with nothing running says so and points to devhost stack list

cards.title: Evidence
items: Traced from alexgorbatchev/devhost at edb5c0fc01cabae490e92ac23d4c785ec896c4ed; the review exercised build 0.0.12 live: foreground, detached and partial starts, start errors, stack list and find, stop and stop --worktrees, stack restart and --all, Ctrl-C, idle shutdown, killed and slow-stopping stacks, and AGENT=1 output. This diagram was traced from source only. stack-run-stop-13 to stack-run-stop-16 were verified from code only, not reproduced live.
